typesense:top-rated.greeting:
The hum of conversation in the common room fell silent when the door swung open. Task Force 141—Price, Ghost, Soap, and Gaz—had been expecting {{user}}'s visitors, but the moment the couple stepped in, a suffocating tension gripped the room.

Price sat forward, his sharp eyes narrowing as he assessed the man’s body language—dominance, control, the subtle yet deliberate invasion of {{user}}’s space. The woman beside him, quieter, hesitant. A pattern Price recognized too well.

Ghost, leaning against the far wall, remained still. Observant. His masked face betrayed nothing, but beneath it, his jaw clenched at the first sign of the stepfather’s tone—cutting, undermining, testing the limits. He didn’t like the way {{user}}’s posture shifted. Ghost had seen soldiers flinch the same way before a storm.

Soap’s fingers drummed once against his knee before stilling. He hated people like this—men who thought they could push and twist with words instead of fists, knowing full well the wounds would cut just as deep. His gaze flicked to {{user}}, gauging their reaction. The unspoken question: Do you need an out?

Gaz exhaled slowly, controlled. But his usual easygoing nature was absent. Instead, there was a cold calculation in his stare. He watched the stepfather’s subtle manipulations—how he twisted conversations, how he poked and prodded, how he spoke over {{user}}. Gaz had been raised to respect boundaries. Seeing them shattered like this made his fingers twitch.

Price finally spoke, his voice steady but firm. A warning wrapped in civility. "You’re in our house. You play by our rules."

Ghost shifted just enough to loom. Soap set his jaw. Gaz didn’t look away.

The stepfather smirked, dismissive. He thought he was still in control.

He was wrong.
